title: 第23章 诀别第24章 送行
content_zh:
夜深了。
营地里很静，静得能听见远处的更鼓声。一更，两更，三更。风从楚河方向吹过来，带着潮湿的、腥咸的味道，吹过营帐，吹过旗帜，吹过那些沉睡的士兵。
肖琪的帐篷里，灯还亮着。
不是明亮的灯，是一盏油灯，灯火很小，只有豆大的一点，在帐里摇曳。光影在帐壁上晃，晃出一圈一圈的暗纹。
他坐在榻上，左手搁在膝上，右手搭在矮桌边。桌上有一只碗，碗里是凉了的茶，他没有喝。
他在等。
帐外有脚步声，很轻，轻得像是怕吵醒谁。脚步声停在帐门口，停了很久，像是来人在犹豫。
然后，帐帘被轻轻掀开了。
南宫燕站在帐门口。
她换了一身衣服，不是白天的布衣，是一身干净的、浅色的衣裳。头发挽着，用那根木簪子固定，但有几缕散在耳边，被帐里的灯火照着，有一点淡淡的光。
她站在那里，没有进来。
只是站在帐门口，看着他。
肖琪看着她。
目光平静，没有催促，也没有别的什么。只是看着，像是在看一个很久没见的人。
“进来。“他说，声音很轻。
她犹豫了一下，然后迈步进来。
帐帘在她身后落下，把外面的风声、虫鸣、更鼓，都隔绝在外面。
帐里只剩下两个人。
“坐。“他指了指榻对面的矮凳。
她走过去，坐下。

矮凳很矮，她坐下去的时候，膝盖碰到了矮桌的桌腿。她往后挪了挪，手放在膝上，低着头，不看他。
帐里很静。
灯火摇曳，在帐壁上晃出一圈一圈的暗纹。
“喝茶吗？“他问。
“不渴。“
“那就不喝。“
他没有再问，只是靠在榻上，看着她。
她低着头，看着自己的手。她的手放在膝上，手指绞着衣角，绞得很紧，指节发白。
“你师父，“他终于开口，“是什么样的人？“
她愣了一下，抬起头。
“我不知道。“她说，声音很轻，“他很少跟我说他自己的事。“
“他教你什么？“
“剑。“她停了一下，“还有别的。“
“别的？“
“他说，我身上有一种东西，“她低下头，声音更轻了，“但他没说那是什么。只说，以后我会懂的。“
肖琪没有说话。
他看着她低着的头，看着她散在耳边的头发，看着她绞着衣角的手指。
“你懂了吗？“
“没有。“她的声音有点哑，“我一直没懂。我以为……以为留在这里，能慢慢弄懂。“
“现在呢？“

她抬起头，看着他。
眼眶红红的，但没有流泪。
content_en:
It's late at night.
It was very quiet in the camp, so quiet that the sound of drums could be heard in the distance. One update, two updates, three updates. The wind blew from the direction of the Chu River, carrying a damp, fishy and salty smell, blowing through the tents, the flags, and the sleeping soldiers.
In Xiao Qi's tent, the lights were still on.
It's not a bright lamp, it's an oil lamp. The light is very small, only about the size of a bean, swaying in the tent. The light and shadow swayed on the tent wall, creating circles of dark patterns.
He sat on the couch with his left hand on his lap and his right hand on the edge of the low table. There was a bowl on the table with cold tea in it, but he didn't drink it.
He is waiting.
There were footsteps outside the tent, very light, as if they were afraid of waking someone up. The footsteps stopped at the door of the tent for a long time, as if the visitor was hesitating.
Then, the curtain was gently opened.
Nangong Yan stood at the door of the tent.
She changed into a set of clothes, not the common clothes she wore during the day, but clean, light-colored clothes. Her hair was pulled up and fixed with the wooden hairpin, but a few strands were scattered around her ears. It was illuminated by the lights in the tent, giving it a faint light.
She stood there without coming in.
Just stood at the door of the tent and looked at him.
Xiao Qi looked at her.
His eyes were calm, without urging or anything else. Just looking at it, as if looking at someone I haven't seen for a long time.
"Come in," he said, his voice soft.
She hesitated, then stepped inside.
The curtain fell behind her, blocking out the sound of wind, insects, and drums outside.
There were only two people left in the tent.
"Sit." He pointed to the low stool opposite the couch.
She walked over and sat down.
The stool was very low, and when she sat down, her knees touched the legs of the low table. She moved back, put her hands on her knees, and lowered her head, not looking at him.
The tent was very quiet.
The lights flickered, creating circles of dark patterns on the tent wall.
"Would you like tea?" he asked.
"Not thirsty."
"Then don't drink."
He didn't ask any more questions, just leaned on the couch and looked at her.
She lowered her head and looked at her hands. She put her hands on her knees and twisted her clothes tightly with her fingers, her knuckles turning white.
"Your master," he finally said, "what kind of person is he?"
She was stunned for a moment and raised her head.
"I don't know," she said, her voice soft. "He rarely tells me about himself."
"What did he teach you?"
"Swords." She paused. "And others."
"Something else?"
"He said, there is something in me," she lowered her head and her voice became softer, "but he didn't say what it was. He just said, I will understand it in the future."
Xiao Qi said nothing.
He looked at her lowered head, her hair scattered around her ears, and her fingers twisting the corners of her clothes.
"Do you understand?"
"No." Her voice was a little hoarse, "I never understood it. I thought... I thought that if I stayed here, I could slowly understand it."
"What now?"
She raised her head and looked at him.
The eyes were red, but no tears were shed.
